title: Korean winter survival item: 전기장판 🥶→🫠 #learnkorean
caption:
전기장판 (jeon-gi-jang-pan) = electric heating mat 🔥
Word by word: 전기 (jeon-gi) = electricity + 장판 (jang-pan) = the vinyl floor covering of a Korean room.
Korean homes heat the floor, not the air — and a 전기장판 is a little heated floor you can sleep on.

Words in this video:
추워 (chu-wo) = I’m cold
따뜻해 (tta-tteu-tae) = it’s warm
못 일어나 (mo-di-reo-na) = I can’t get up
포기 (po-gi) = I give up

pinnedComment: What keeps YOU warm in winter? 👇 (a heater? hot tea? a 전기장판? 😆)
alt: A needle-felt miniature Korean studio apartment on a freezing night, −12°C and no heater. Mongle, a coral felt ghost-like mascot, shivers under a grey knitted blanket on a cream quilted mat and says 추, 추워 (so cold). In a close-up it presses the mat’s controller with its body; the light turns orange, the mat glows and Mongle says 아~ 따뜻해 (ahh, so warm), then slowly melts flat like cheese: 녹는다 (I’m melting). A card shows 전기장판, jeon-gi-jang-pan, electric heating mat. Next morning the alarm phone rings; Mongle says 일어나야지 (gotta get up) and tries three times to get up, stretching up like melted cheese — 못 일어나 (I can’t get up!) — then splats flat again and says 포기 (I give up). The end shows 전기장판 in big letters and asks what keeps you warm in winter.
